source_text: Verum tali expositione, qua quidem nec pervertere sensum nec suffugere valebis, tamen non solum praestigias tuas, sed etiam illius, quam in nos inflammabas, figmentum invidiae perdidisti. Graviter quippe nos in fidem commisisse iactabas, qui dicimus gratiam quidem Christi uniformiter esse tradendam nec debere verba eius et instituta concuti, sed aequaliter cunctis a se imbutis adoptionis et sanctificationis promotionisque dona conferre, verum non omnes accedentes in unis reatibus invenire, sed eos quidem, qui propria voluntate peccaverint, sine cuius opere nullum potest esse peccatum, liberare de reatu et de malis facere bonos, innocentes autem infucata primaevitate felices pro nullo opere malae voluntatis arguere, cuius apud eos novit experientiam non fuisse.
pass_a_gloss: But by such an exposition, by which indeed you will be able neither to pervert the sense nor to flee, you have nevertheless lost not only your juggler's tricks but also the fiction of that envy which you were inflaming against us. For you were boasting that we had committed gravely against the faith, we who say that the grace of Christ is indeed to be handed down uniformly and that its words and ordinances ought not to be shaken, but that it confers equally on all imbued by it the gifts of adoption and of sanctification and of promotion, but that it does not find all approaching in one reatus, but those indeed who have sinned by their own will, without whose work there can be no sin, it frees from reatus and makes good from evil, but innocent ones happy with an unpainted first-age it accuses for no work of an evil will, of which it has known that there was not experience with them.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But with this explanation—which will not enable you either to distort the meaning or to escape—you have lost not only your tricks but also the manufactured hostility you were inflaming against us. You used to claim that we gravely offended against the faith by saying this: Christ’s grace must indeed be administered uniformly, and its words and institutions must not be unsettled. It confers the gifts of adoption, sanctification, and advancement equally on all whom it initiates. Yet it does not find everyone who approaches it in the same state of guilt. Those who have sinned by their own will—without whose activity no sin can exist—it frees from guilt and makes good out of evil. But it does not accuse the innocent, blessed in the unstained freshness of their first age, of any act of an evil will, since it knows they have had no experience of such a will.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
